notes:
Report 1 (ledger detail) actually resolves last night's big worry in Tidewick's favor: the "credit = payment + refund" pattern is correct double-entry accounting, not double-counted revenue. On capture: Sales revenue (credit) + VAT payable (credit) = Payment gateway clearing (debit). On refund: Refunds and returns/contra-revenue (debit) + VAT payable (debit) = Payment gateway clearing (credit) — e.g. Ampfeld Elektronik #1727 and every other refunded sample shows this exact structure, balanced to the cent. My "ledger_credit_total" diagnostic from Night 2 was simply summing credits across unrelated accounts (revenue credits at capture + clearing credits at refund), which is apples-to-oranges — the ledger itself is fine. Report 2's scale-up confirms this: 78.55% + 18.74% ≈ 97.3% of 2025's captured payments follow one of these two clean, explainable patterns. That's good news I can tell Tobias with confidence.

Two smaller things still need a next step before I call #1 fully done: (a) "other mismatch" is 249 payments / €84,443 in payment value (2.1% of count) — Castell Fasteners' SO-100233 in the detail report hints these may be non-gateway payment methods (bank transfer) where VAT/revenue nets differently than my simple gross/net comparison expected, not a real error, but I want to confirm that before saying so; (b) "no ledger entries" is small in money (€3,380 across 67 payments, 0.58%) but is a genuine audit-trail gap spread across 31 merchants — worth knowing whether it's an old, fixed bug or still happening now, since "we found gaps but can't tell if they're ongoing" is a weak answer to give auditors.

Tonight's three slots: characterize the "other mismatch" bucket by payment method (test the bank-transfer/B2B hypothesis); redo the revenue reconciliation using the *correct* ledger accounts (Sales/Shipping revenue credits minus Refunds-and-returns debits, compared to payments' net amount) so I have a trustworthy "yes, it ties out" statement built the right way instead of my flawed Night 2 shortcut; and trend the no-ledger-entries gap by month to see if it's historical or still occurring.

requests.title: Other-Mismatch Payments: Characterization by Payment Method, 2025
requests.question: Is the 2.1%-of-payments 'other mismatch' ledger bucket explained by a specific payment method (e.g. bank transfer/wire rather than card/gateway), or is it unexplained?
requests.grain: one payment_methods.kind, restricted to 2025 payments in the 'other mismatch' reconciliation category
columns: avg_abs_diff_eur (average of |ledger_credit_total_eur - expected_eur| where expected is the nearer of net_amount or payment+refund)
requests.details: Recompute the same classification as last night's 'Ledger-to-Payment Reconciliation Pattern at Scale, 2025' report: for payments captured in 2025 (status captured/refunded/partially_refunded), aggregate linked ledger_entries by payment_id (sum of direction='credit' amounts, each converted to EUR via exchange_rates on the ledger entry's own currency_code and date(occurred_at)), and compare to payment_amount_eur and amount_refunded_eur (converted via exchange_rates on captured_at). A payment falls in 'other mismatch' if its ledger credit total is NOT within 1% (or €1, whichever is larger) of either (payment_amount_eur - amount_refunded_eur) or (payment_amount_eur + amount_refunded_eur), and it has at least one ledger_entries row (i.e., exclude 'no ledger entries' payments). For that 'other mismatch' set only, join payments.payment_method_id -> payment_methods.kind and group by kind (null/missing payment_method_id as 'unknown'). avg_abs_diff_eur = average of the absolute difference between ledger_credit_total_eur and whichever of the two expected values (net or gross+refund) is closer. Order by payment_count descending.
builds_on: Ledger Line-Item Detail for Flagged Sample Payments, 2025

requests.title: 2025 Revenue Reconciliation via Correct Ledger Accounts, by Quarter
requests.question: Using the right ledger accounts (revenue credits net of refund contra-revenue debits), does the ledger's net revenue tie to the payments table's net captured amount each quarter?
columns: ledger_revenue_credit_eur (sum of ledger_entries.amount, direction='credit', for ledger_accounts.account_type='revenue', occurred_at in the quarter)
payments_net_amount_eur (sum of payments.amount - payments.amount_refunded for payments captured_at in the quarter, status captured/refunded/partially_refunded)
requests.details: Source: ledger_entries joined to ledger_accounts for account_type, filtered to occurred_at in calendar year 2025, converting each ledger_entries.amount to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=ledger_entries.currency_code, as_of=date(occurred_at)). Separately, payments filtered to captured_at in 2025 with the usual status filter, converting amount and amount_refunded to EUR via exchange_rates on captured_at. Group both sides by calendar quarter and join on quarter. diff_eur = ledger_net_revenue_eur - payments_net_amount_eur; diff_pct = diff_eur / payments_net_amount_eur * 100. Order chronologically 2025-Q1 to 2025-Q4 (4 rows).
builds_on: Ledger Line-Item Detail for Flagged Sample Payments, 2025

requests.title: No-Ledger-Entries Gap Trend by Month, 2025
requests.question: Is the small 'payment with zero ledger entries' gap an ongoing issue in current operations, or was it confined to earlier in the year and since resolved?
requests.details: Source: payments with status captured/refunded/partially_refunded and captured_at in 2025, LEFT JOIN to a per-payment count of linked ledger_entries via payment_id. Convert payment amounts to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=payments.currency_code, as_of=date(captured_at)). Group by calendar month of captured_at. amount_at_risk_eur sums payment_amount_eur only for payments with zero linked ledger_entries. Order chronologically 2025-01 to 2025-12 (12 rows).
builds_on: Payments With No Ledger Entries, by Merchant, 2025
